elements.element: The licence extends to Customer's affiliates.
elements.evidence: The grant expressly covers “affiliated companies of Sparkling” operating at Authorized Locations.

elements.element: The licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
elements.evidence: The grant expressly includes “contractors acting on their behalf” operating at Authorized Locations.
The clause does not state that paid-up licences are perpetual, and the absence of paid-up licences is not demonstrable from the operative language.
The clause does not state that paid-up licences are irrevocable, and the absence of paid-up licences is not demonstrable from the operative language.

elements.element: A subscription licence may be terminated only for material breach.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no restriction limiting termination of a subscription licence to material breach, and the absence of subscription licences is not demonstrable.

elements.element: A subscription licence may be terminated for material breach only if that breach remains uncured.
elements.evidence: The clause provides neither a cure requirement nor an uncured-breach trigger for termination.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to any successor of Customer.
elements.evidence: Transferability is limited to a successor connected with specified M&A events, rather than extending to successors generally.

elements.element: The licence extends to Customer's affiliates upon written notice.
elements.evidence: Affiliated companies are covered automatically, without a notice condition; this is broader and more favorable than coverage upon written notice.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.
elements.evidence: The clause permits transfer to a successor in connection with a merger, amalgamation, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all of Sparkling's assets.

result.reason: The redline satisfies the fallback because affiliates already receive automatic coverage and transfer is permitted to an M&A successor. It does not satisfy the preferred position because it omits perpetual and irrevocable treatment for paid-up licences, omits the required subscription-termination standard, and limits successor transferability to M&A events. It preserves the Authorized Location, object-code, non-exclusive, and additional-fee limitations. It is not minimal relative to the completed fallback because contractor coverage was added even though it was unnecessary to achieve that level and the remaining preferred requirements were not completed.
